title: White & Case announces global rollout of Legora across 43 offices
author: Legora

dom.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training

st.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training
st.an: The source directly supports the platform-led adoption proposition: White & Case plans a global rollout while combining Legora with internal development, joint product work and an explicit focus on adoption. It describes anticipated workflow and client benefits rather than demonstrated productivity, accuracy or client outcomes.

kp.k: Global deployment targets all lawyers, regions and practices
kp.d: The December 18, 2025 announcement reports White & Case's planned global rollout of Legora to all lawyers across 43 offices in 29 countries, covering the Americas, EMEA and Asia Pacific. The stated aims are faster review, improved drafting and deeper research, including support for complex, high-stakes matters; these are deployment objectives rather than reported performance findings.
qs: White & Case selected Legora as a strategic partner to help its lawyers review faster, draft smarter, and research deeper with advanced AI-driven capabilities.
The rollout will extend to all lawyers across White & Case’s global platform.

The firm operates in 43 offices across 29 countries in the Americas, EMEA and Asia Pacific regions, and is widely recognized as one of the world’s global elite law firms, with top-tier practices spanning mergers and acquisitions, disputes, capital markets, financial restructuring and insolvency and more.
Under the partnership, White & Case will roll out Legora’s AI platform globally to strengthen legal workflows and support complex, high-stakes matters.

kp.k: Firm strategy combines external partnerships with internal development
kp.d: In a customer quotation carried by Legora, White & Case partner and Executive Committee member Dipen Sabharwal describes a strategy combining legal-technology partnerships with custom internal solutions. He highlights collaboration and adaptation of the vendor platform to the firm's needs, framing the partnership as enabling firm personnel to develop solutions for clients.
qs: This partnership is part of our strategic approach to AI and innovation, which combines partnering with market leading legal technology companies while also building custom internal solutions.
We are impressed by Legora's pace of innovation, openness to collaboration, and commitment to shaping its platform to our needs.
We are excited by the opportunities for everyone at our Firm to create solutions that serve our clients and empower our people.

kp.k: Joint products target law firm–in-house collaboration
kp.d: The announcement says White & Case and Legora will collaborate on new products and solutions beyond platform deployment, including the Legora Portal, announced earlier that fall. Its intended role is to change collaboration between law firms and in-house legal teams and deliver additional client value through AI-enabled workflows; no resulting outcomes are reported.
qs: Beyond the deployment, White & Case and Legora will collaborate on new products and solutions, including the Legora Portal – announced earlier this fall – designed to transform collaboration between law firms and in-house legal teams and help deliver additional value to law firm clients through AI-enabled workflows.

kp.k: Adoption is presented as essential to organisational change
kp.d: Legora CEO and co-founder Max Junestrand presents adoption and implementation effort as necessary for change at White & Case's scale. His remarks distinguish an initial partnership phase from the forthcoming global rollout and express an ambition to help lawyers use AI to focus on client outcomes, rather than reporting measured improvements.
qs: Together, we’ll develop the future of AI-driven legal work and enable their teams to leverage AI to focus on what matters most: delivering consistent, world-class quality outcomes for clients at a global scale,
Real change at this scale requires a lot of hard work and a focus on adoption.
We look forward to entering the next stage to ensure the global rollout is successful.

kp.k: Vendor reports growth and forecasts further international expansion
kp.d: Legora reports growing from 40 to 250 team members over the preceding 12 months, across six named cities, and supporting tens of thousands of lawyers daily at 600 customers in more than 50 markets. Separately, it forecasts more than doubling in size and opening additional global hubs in the year ahead. These are vendor-reported scale figures and forward-looking expansion expectations.
qs: Over the past 12 months, Legora has grown from 40 to 250 team members across Stockholm, London, New York, Denver, Sydney and Bengaluru.
Today, the Legora platform supports tens of thousands of lawyers every day at 600 customers in more than 50 markets.
In the year ahead, Legora expects to more than double in size and open additional global hubs, further strengthening its ability to serve a rapidly expanding international client base.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Legora’s announcement presents global AI deployment as a way to improve lawyers’ review, drafting and research, support high-stakes work, and change collaboration with clients.
pts.d: The Legora newsroom reports that White & Case selected its platform to improve review speed, drafting and research and will deploy it to all lawyers globally. It describes planned joint product development, including the Legora Portal, as intended to transform collaboration between law firms and in-house teams and deliver additional client value. White & Case Executive Committee member Dipen Sabharwal places the partnership within a strategy combining external legal technology with custom internal solutions and anticipates opportunities to create client-serving solutions. Legora CEO Max Junestrand predicts that the partnership will enable teams to focus on consistent, high-quality client outcomes at global scale. These are announced deployment plans and intended benefits, rather than reported measurements of improvements. Separately, Legora reports growing adoption and forecasts further expansion of its own business.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The source offers an announced partnership, executive accounts and company-reported scale figures, but no measured legal-work performance outcomes.
pts.d: The concrete deployment case is White & Case’s announced rollout across 43 offices in 29 countries. Sabharwal cites impressions of Legora’s innovation, collaboration and willingness to tailor the platform; Junestrand cites experience with the initial partnership phase. Legora reports employee growth from 40 to 250 over the preceding 12 months and daily platform support for tens of thousands of lawyers at 600 customers in more than 50 markets. These figures describe vendor growth and adoption, not demonstrated gains in review speed, drafting quality, research depth or client outcomes. The announcement supplies no benchmarks, comparative results, quantified productivity gains or client-value measurements supporting those intended benefits.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The December 18, 2025 announcement describes a forthcoming global rollout without a completion date; successful change is explicitly linked to adoption effort.
pts.d: The rollout and joint product development are prospective as of publication, following an initial partnership phase. The Portal had been announced earlier in fall 2025, but no implementation or benefits-realisation deadline is supplied. Junestrand states that change at this scale requires hard work and attention to adoption. Sabharwal also emphasises collaboration and tailoring the platform to firm needs. The employee-growth figures concern the preceding 12 months; Legora’s prediction that it will more than double in size and open more hubs concerns the year ahead, approximately 2026. The source does not specify a precise metric for the forecast increase in size.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The claimed beneficiaries are lawyers throughout a large global law firm, its clients and their in-house legal teams; Legora also anticipates expanding its international service capacity.
pts.d: White & Case is described as an Am Law 10 firm, with deployment covering all lawyers, regions and practices across its 43 offices and 29 countries. Intended workflow improvements therefore span transactional, disputes and other complex legal work rather than a single pilot team. Lawyers are positioned as users whose work AI supports, not as roles explicitly slated for replacement. Clients are promised additional value and consistent quality, while in-house legal teams are the buyer-side participants in the Portal’s proposed collaboration changes. Legora is the software provider and joint development partner, with planned business expansion intended to support its growing international customer base. The source makes no concrete claim about staffing reductions, fees or access to justice.
